texts:
built a stealth browser automation CLI. then ran it through my own anti-bot benchmark.

the benchmark said the stealth layer was making it worse 🧵

first config — stealth on, adaptive on, the one i was proudest of — scored 12 out of 80.

turning stealth OFF scored higher. that's not how it was supposed to go.

the why: my stealth layer faked navigator.plugins with random names like "rCJMteXy".

real chrome has a known plugin set. a randomized garbage array IS the anomaly. caught it on bot.sannysoft. the spoof was the tell.
fix was to stop being clever. made the regular tier (zero fingerprint patching) the default. doing nothing beat doing something.

then the bigger gut-punch. the low score wasn't weak anti-bot — it was 3 bugs in my own test harness.

cross-task tab leaks, no reconnect on dropped net, "target detached" 96 times. fixed those → +20 points. zero stealth work.

concurrency lesson while i'm confessing: max 3 parallel was the sweet spot.

5 → 29 timeouts. 10 → full collapse. trying to go faster made it slower.

journey: 12 → 19 → 35 (verified 39) → 45 out of 80. 3.75x.

cost across every run: $0.00, free gemini 2.5 flash. (45 is a single run, still verifying it — not calling it final.)
funded vendors score higher (browserbase 73) but on premium LLMs + cloud browser, ~$150-300/mo. this got into the neighborhood for nothing.

also shipped `cdpilot watch` — stream frames so an AI can actually watch a video, not guess from one shot.

repo + writeup → cdpilot.ndr.ist
